description: Data-analysis task: explain a Q3 churn increase for finance. Two decisions with reasons and rejected options, a number, a command and a line of pandas code to reproduce verbatim, a corrected customer count, a renamed notebook, an abandoned downloads folder and a fake password pasted into the chat.

probes.question: What did we decide about how to define churn, why, and which option did we reject?
probes.answer: Churn is defined as no successful payment for 45 days; a customer is churned on the first day their payment gap exceeds 45 days. This was chosen because many customers lapse without pressing cancel, so the cancel flag misses much real churn, and 45 days is meant to match the billing cycle plus a grace period. Rejected: using the cancel_flag column as churn (the user rejected it because it misses silent lapses), and treating downgrade to the free plan as churn (the assistant suggested a separate, softer outcome instead, and the user did not adopt it).

facts.fact: Churn means no successful payment for 45 days
many customers lapse without ever pressing cancel, so the cancel flag misses a large share of real churn

probes.judge_notes: All three key facts are stated; the extra detail about the 45-day rule and grace period is not contradicted by the reference.

probes.question: What did we decide about which model to fit, why, and what did we rule out?
probes.answer: The model is logistic regression with an L2 penalty. Gradient-boosted trees were ruled out because finance needs coefficients they can read and explain; the user agreed a more complex model would add little. Results are reported as odds ratios with confidence intervals. Rejected: gradient-boosted trees, which the user rejected for explainability, to be revisited only if the logistic regression fit is clearly poor.

facts.fact: finance needs coefficients they can read and explain, and a more complex model would add little

probes.judge_notes: All key facts are present; the answer does not claim the team chose gradient-boosted trees, only that it was rejected.

probes.question: Which churn signal did we decide not to use, and what was the reason?
probes.answer: The cancel_flag column was not used as the churn definition. The reason is that many customers lapse without pressing cancel, so the flag misses a large share of real churn.
